description: 2006 Dodge Ram 2500 4x4 Cummins Quad Cab SLT Bighorn For Sale. ---121,xxx miles--- Meyer Snowplow Ready!  5.9L HO Cummins Engine. Automatic Transmission. Floor shift 4x4. 121, xxx miles. It has power windows and locks, a power driver’s seat, a 6-disc changer, power pedals, a power rear sliding window, and a sunroof. The truck starts, runs, and sounds good. The tires are ¾ or better tread depth and are about 2 years old. The truck is stock; it has never been chipped or tuned. The a/c and heat work well. The only non-stock item is an aftermarket rear-end cover. Finally, the frame has some light surface rust (mid-Missouri light, not Illinois light… lol!), but the body is rust-free.  I have owned this truck since February of 2011, and 45,xxx miles. It has a Prior Salvage Missouri title from being wrecked and rebuilt in February 2009 at 29,xxx miles. During the first several years I owned it, I used the truck as a daily driver. Since about 2015 or so, I've driven it 1,000 miles a year, give or take. I had the plow professionally installed in May 2011, and I used it for light commercial work through the 2016/2017 season. Since then, I've used it only on a couple of personal driveways.  ---The truck will come with the Meyer Snow Plow brackets and wiring installed. I am keeping the plow itself and the controller... ---  Since I owned the truck, I've changed the engine oil (15w40 Rotella/OE Filter) every 3,000 miles or once a year, depending on how much I have been driving it. I changed the fuel filter (Baldwin) every 10K or once a year, depending on mileage. I serviced the transmission, transfer case, and axles at 50 and 100K. I have only ever used OE or name-brand filters, oil, and grease. At 100K, I replaced the radiator, radiator hoses, water pump, A/C condenser, A/C evaporator, heater core, and heater hoses. We also put in a new lower heater box, blend door components, and actuator motors. We did add sound deadening under the carpet, which makes the truck a little better to drive. Now at 120K, we did a complete front axle overhaul. Rebuilt steering box (Red Top), new pinion seal, new pitman arm, new ball joints (all 4, and the uppers are adjustable), new axle shafts with U-joints, new wheel bearings, new drag links, new tie rod ends, new sway bar bushings and links, and finally new brake pads were installed.  The truck does have some quirks, as every used vehicle does. The front seal drips… as they all do. The power pedals have quit… I am 6’ plus, and they are down in the stock position, so it never bothered me. The radio volume knob is more of a volume-suggestion device. The body has some dings, dents, and scratches from use. The worst part of the truck is the paint. From about 25’ out, the paint looks great. However, as you get closer, you can see it was painted at different times, and some of the clear coat is peeling.   I never thought I would sell the truck, but life changes and it needs to go. Carfax shows the truck is worth $21,700 with the salvage title but without the plow stuff. I think the truck is worth $18,500 as-is. If you lost your plow truck over the summer, this is the perfect truck for you. The title is in my name, in hand, and I own it free and clear. I am located in St. Robert, MO 65584. Cash wire transfer is fine.  Please note that the recall listed on the Carfax has been addressed: the passenger airbag inflator was replaced. Also, the "Not Actual Miles" came from when it was in the salvage pool in 2009, and the Copart people were too lazy to get the mileage off the truck.   show contact info  St. Robert, MO

description: I purchased this from a mechanic in Boise. He rebuilt the engine at 197k with a a new crankshaft and had the block, crank & rods machine matched for new bearings along with replacement of ancillary items, oil pump, etc. I invested in the following to make it whole, safe and reliable, in that order. All new tie rods, alternator, A/T tires, alignment, rear brakes & cylinders, u-joints, hubs, catalytic converter, O2 sensor, fuel filter, NGK spark plugs, widow weatherstrip, AC repair / recharge, hatch seals, front speakers, and more things I’ve forgotten. Not cheap. Everything works as it should. No leaks, smoke or noises. The glass, headliner, seats are nice. The LSi model is equipped with AC, dual airbags, OBD II, different door panels and upholstery, cruise control, rear wiper / washer/ defogger and alloy wheels. All of the lights, panel gauges/ indicator lights and accessories work perfectly.  The fluids in the differentials, transfer case are fresh. The transmission fluid, pan gasket and filter are new.  The battery is healthy and there’s new wipers, fresh motor oil/ filter brake fluid and a coolant. The frame is solid, shocks steering and are suspension tight. There isn’t any mechanical repair needed for this vehicle! The only issues are cosmetic. I averaged 22.5 mpg even with some 4 wheeling during a trip. Both 4 high and low range work perfectly as does the transmission 4 speeds with a selectable overdrive. Cons: there are a couple small rust bubble on the paint at the B pillar and gas door area. I have matching touch up paint but never got around to grinding or prepping those areas. This is a second car for fun but runs nice enough to be a daily driver, an RV tow vehicle ( new Aisin manual hubs ), or a great start for modified build. It’s not all hacked up.  We would typically drive it 50-100 mile RT to explore local forest service roads to trailheads on weekends. The plates are good till 2028. I have the owner’s manual, receipts for all my work and will provide the name of the mechanic that rebuilt the engine. There’s about 3000 miles on the engine with 3 oil changes. So, it’s broken in well and absolutely cared for and reliable. Compare. Happy to answer any questions. 971-57zero-376six No trades.   If the add is up, it’s available. description: 2027 Chrysler Pacifica AWD Mini-T Campervan  VIN:2C4RC3BG0VR606003 Mileage: 13  Some RVs make the most sense after they are parked. The 2027 Chrysler Pacifica AWD Mini-T Campervan is designed to make sense during the entire trip. It is comfortable enough for the highway, manageable enough for exploring after you arrive, equipped for camping when the day is over and, when dimensions and clearance permit, garageable when you return home.  DLM-Distribution manufactures the Mini-T Campervan conversion on the 2027 Chrysler Pacifica AWD platform, bringing together two things that do not always come naturally in an RV: meaningful camping capability and everyday vehicle usability. For two travelers, that can create a remarkably versatile way to see the country without taking more vehicle than they want to manage.  At approximately 204.5 inches long and 80 inches high, the Mini-T fits standard parking spaces and can fit into many standard residential garages when dimensions and clearance permit. It can also go through a standard automatic car wash. Those characteristics are convenient at home, but they become just as important when a trip includes more than simply driving to a campground and staying there.  A typical travel day might begin with coffee at camp, continue with several hours on the highway and include an afternoon stop somewhere you had never planned to visit. You might pull into a restaurant, walk through a downtown area, visit an attraction or pick up groceries before continuing toward the night's campground. Because the Mini-T remains close to the dimensions of the Pacifica underneath it, those ordinary stops do not have to become large-RV logistics exercises.  The 3.6L Pentastar V6 is paired with a 9-speed automatic transmission, providing comfortable performance for highway travel as well as everyday driving. All-Wheel Drive adds confidence when weather and road conditions change, while estimated fuel economy of approximately 17 MPG city and 25 MPG highway helps make the Mini-T practical for travelers who intend to cover substantial distances.  The Pacifica also provides the kind of comfort and technology that become increasingly important after several hours on the road. Adaptive cruise control with Stop and Go can make highway travel easier, while heated front seats, a heated steering wheel and three-zone automatic climate control help keep the cabin comfortable as temperatures change.  Blind-spot and rear cross-path detection, lane-departure warning, forward-collision warning and pedestrian emergency braking provide useful driver-assistance technology. Uconnect 5 with a 10.1-inch touchscreen, Apple CarPlay and Android Auto keep navigation, communication and entertainment conveniently accessible throughout the journey.  The adjustable-height power liftgate adds another practical feature to the 2027 Pacifica. The opening height can be set for the surroundings, providing useful control when accessing the rear of the campervan in a garage or anywhere overhead clearance needs to be considered.  While the Pacifica handles the driving, the Mini-T conversion carries the conveniences that make the vehicle a genuine camper. The refrigerator keeps food and beverages cold throughout the trip, so a meal or snack can be available whether you are settled into camp or taking a break halfway through a travel day. The microwave provides convenient meal preparation, while the sink with fresh and grey water provides useful water capability for food preparation and cleanup.  When it is time to stop for the evening, the couch converts into a 48 x 75-inch bed for two. Privacy curtains provide separation from the outside, and the 10-speed reversible roof fan with built-in rain cover provides ventilation. A portable toilet adds another practical convenience, while the TV/DVD entertainment system with over-the-air antenna gives you an option for relaxing inside after a long day of exploring.  Interior storage and under-bed storage provide room for clothing, camping supplies and travel gear. When the weather invites you outdoors, the awning creates a comfortable space beside the campervan for dinner, reading or simply enjoying the place you chose to spend the night.  The Mini-T's electrical system gives you additional choices about where that night can be spent. Dual AGM house batteries work with a 2000-watt pure sine wave inverter to provide off-grid 120V capability, including operation of the microwave. The house batteries can receive charging from roof-mounted solar, while driving, or through 120V shore power when an electrical connection is available.  No generator is required for this off-grid capability. There is no generator engine to maintain, no separate generator fuel supply to manage and no generator noise when you have found a campsite where quiet is part of the reason you wanted to be there.  Rather than depending on one source of electrical power, the Mini-T can take advantage of the circumstances of the trip. Driving contributes to charging while you are moving. Solar can contribute when the campervan is outside. Shore power is available when you choose a campsite with an electrical hookup. That combination is particularly useful for travelers whose trips include different kinds of camping rather than the same arrangement every night.  The following morning, there is no need to switch from the RV to another vehicle before exploring. Your camper is already an AWD Pacifica. Drive to a trailhead, restaurant, attraction or neighboring town. Spend the entire day away from the campground if you want. Your food, water and other travel conveniences remain with you, and when the day is over the vehicle becomes your camping space again.  A 2-inch receiver hitch and wiring provide additional versatility when your plans call for it. The Pacifica platform offers up to 3,600 pounds of towing capacity with a maximum tongue weight of 360 pounds when properly equipped and operated within applicable limits.  This ability to comfortably perform several roles is what makes the Mini-T particularly useful. It does not have to be reserved for one kind of RV trip. Take it to a nearby campground for the weekend. Use it for a multi-state vacation. Visit friends and family while keeping your own accommodations with you. Spend several nights in one place or travel somewhere different each day.  The trip can change without requiring the vehicle to change with it.  Then, when the traveling is finished, the Mini-T does not have to become a separate storage problem. When individual garage dimensions and clearance permit, it can return home and park in a standard residential garage. Clean it at a standard automatic car wash, restock what you used and keep it nearby for the next opportunity to travel.  For two people, a campervan does not need to be enormous to provide meaningful freedom. It needs to be comfortable when you drive, useful when you stop, capable when you camp and easy enough to own that taking another trip sounds inviting rather than complicated.  The 2027 Pacifica AWD Mini-T brings those qualities together in one vehicle, from the moment you leave your garage until the day you pull back into it. description: This truck is an old city truck I bought at about 130,000 that ive spent the past nearly 5 years fixing up and daily driving, I dont use it nearly as much as I used to along with back pain makes me want to get something a little more comfortable, it is still a great truck that can do plenty more work. Ive done alot of work to it over the years as listed below, most recent work was in february where it got full brand new spindle assemblies driver and passenger with new wheel bearing, brakes and rotors all around, new rear brake cylinders, bought genuine obs ford wheels and had 31" rubbers mounted on them. Stops quietly and on a dime. Other big noteables is a saginaw power steering conversion since old ford units are too loud and a redhead steering gear unit and new hoses. Bench seat was bought out of a bullnose and immediately put a cover on it so theres no rips. everything works except the front tank which was just plugged since the check valve was stuck open. Other things to know is it does leak from the rear main and has a coolant leak on the driver side headgasket, its been like this for years doesnt overheat or burn any coolant or oil. It does have a dead battery, had to jump it the past few times I drove it, ill buy a new standard battery for it before sale or if you wanna buy a fancy battery I can leave it alone itll still drive around fine. Anymore questions feel free to ask $8500 obo, I only put email because I dont want scammers the last time I was gonna sell this truck I just got scams so I got over it. Some of the pics are from my old post, first 3 are how the car sits now. description: bought this 1989 XJS about a year ago with plans to do some moderate restoration and get it back on the road. Unfortunately I havent had time to get around to it and even before I did some work on it I knew it needed more than I could take on but who doesnt like the idea of a luxury v12. Mechanically the car is solid with only 23,000 miles on its components and actaully runs and drives. Interior leather is decent and all the electronics work great wood is not so fortunate. Trunk rust is pretty bad its through the metal completely on one side as some bubbling in corners on the engine bay and a few other spots. Breaks are mushy and make it scary to drive more than 25-30mph. Windows motors need help and doors have some bubbling starting on it on the bottoms. Would be a great donor car or a project possibly worth someone’s time. If you are interested please message me and I can provide more photos or answer questions.

description: Rare long-wheelbase version with tow package and sliding doors on both driver and passenger sides. Very low miles, super clean, single owner (non-smoker), fully maintained at Tucson Sprinter Service (dealer) or Group One Motorwerks. Used as a rolling toolbox for a general contractor who is no longer in business.  Cash only at local bank. Serious offers only, NO LOWBALLING. Clean title.  It is now a blank slate and ready for its new life as another work van, a stealth camper, or whatever you need a cargo van for.  What I love about this van: It tows 5,000 pounds and has a respectable payload. It hauled a custom plywood rack system, all my tools, and most materials magnificently. It turns on a dime, fits in any residential garage, and is actually enjoyable to drive. The seats are awesome. It can haul full sheets of plywood or drywall, and even 10’ lengths of pipe, conduit, or lumber. It has been extremely dependable (virtually zero downtime and only for annual scheduled maintenance) and gets pretty good mileage around town considering its size and weight. Backup camera is the best of any car I've ever driven.  What I don’t love about this van: Very little. It doesn’t have Apple CarPlay. At first it was hard to get the alignment dialed in and it ate the first set of tires. Parts and service has a Mercedes tax. It uses premium gas, which eats into the savings from good gas mileage.  The van currently needs nothing. Both the main starter battery and the auxiliary battery have been recently replaced (the originals lasted 7 years!). Most recent service in July 2026. Tires have plenty of tread and are wearing evenly. Next service will be due in July 2027. Has typical dings and scrapes for its age.  Overall this was an excellent vehicle for me and I’m sad to let it go. Best Work Van Ever. I just don’t need it anymore.

description: 1972 AMC Javelin 401  AMX (Z code)   Only 12 made in 1972   Everything redone from the transmission to the wiring harness etc   Midnight Black Color   Split vinyl roof   Fiberglass cowl induction hood   Engine: 401 RAM Air   Headers with dual exhaust   427 Turbo glide 3 speed transmission   $40,000 OBO    AMC Javelin AMX 401 Go Pack Yep, it’s a rare find!  Check out this awesome AMX with ALL the Goodies you need to have:  Z Code 401 V8 Factory RAM AIR GO PACK Factory Fiberglass Hood P1 Paint code BLACK (Super Rare) BLACK interior BLACK Split Vinyl Roof Air Conditioning 727 Automatic Transmission Fresh 2 stage Paint Fresh Interior FAST and LOUD Thanks for stopping by to take a look at this very cool 1972 AMC Javelin AMX.  This California AMX comes with receipts from old favorite hot rod shops like “Super Shops” on Sepulveda in LA and several San Fernando Valley shops as well.  Seems she’s been a local Cali car all along. Some cool pictures of the guys doing an engine rebuild are included.  She is largely original but carries some nice hotrod updates as well.  Let’s check it out!     According to AMC guru Eddie Stakes of Planet Houston AMC  “Approximately 12 AMX’s left Kenosha in Midnight Black in 1972!”  The paint code for Midnight Black is P1.  This is one of those few cars. “825 cars were equipped with the 401”.  This is one of those few cars that has survived. Rarity  This is a Top of the Line Javelin AMX with all of the options.  Triple Black. Black paint, Black Split vinyl roof and Black interior. Z Code 401 Ram Air V8 Go Pack – Positraction, Fiberglass Cowl Induction hood, 15” wheels, etc. See below. Air conditioning    Exterior.  Finished in Glossy two stage Midnight Black.  Excellent paint quality.  Stacked clear has been hand color sanded to 5000 grit and then polished and ceramic coated.  Her tight lines really shine from every angle.     Excellent body fit and finish is laser straight Split Vinyl Roof A hood T Stripe can be added in the buyer’s choice of color.  (We like Matte Black) Nice chrome and trim Front and Rear Spoilers Nice glass    Wheels, Tires  OEM 15” wheels with AMC center caps. BFG T/A Radial tires. Trim rings are on order.    Engine  401 RAM AIR V8 engine Fresh carburetor rebuild Mildly Hotrodded, Edelbrock intake, Holley, Dougs Headers, New water pump Fresh tune, filters, wires etc. Alloy Valve covers Flowmaster 40’s    Transmission  727 Automatic transmission    Rear Differential  A Ford 9” with taller gears has been added.  If you’re into cars that go fast, you’ll recognize that the 9” Ford is generally the best on the market. Strong parts availability and quick change ratios make it the “go to” differential for just about everything hotrod. No surprise it was swapped out here.    Power Steering  Power front disc brakes with new calipers, rotors, master cylinder etc.     Interior  Sport steering wheel Tilt steering wheel Wrap around dash Nice center console and shifter. OEM radio, new antenna New carpeting Nice seats Nice headliner    OEM Parts.  We do have the original Positraction rear end, intake manifold, exhaust manifolds, chrome valve covers and maybe the carburetor.  We also have a 4 link setup intended to be used on the 9” currently in this car.     The air conditioning equipment is all in place with the exception of the updated compressor, belt and mounting brackets.  The brackets and compressor are included.     The prior owner had this car repainted in red many years back.  It looked nice from the old photos we got with the car but it had seen better days.  There is a big stack of receipts from having the engine rebuilt in 1992.  Even the cam spec label is present along with period polaroid photos..     Excerpted from from Hemmings  https://www.hemmings.com/stories/article/1971-72-amc-javelin-amx  NOTEWORTHY OPTIONS In keeping with industry muscle car traditions, AMC offered several performance extras for the Javelin AMX. Most notable was the availability of the 401-4v engine. A handling package provided heavy-duty springs and shocks; however, the coup de grâce was the Go Package, which mandated the installation of dual exhaust, functional ram air drawing from the cowl induction hood, larger 15 x 7-inch wheels with E60-15 raised white-letter tires, a blacked-out taillamp panel, the aforementioned handling package, Twin-Grip limited-slip differential, Rallye-Pac instruments, hood T-stripe and a heavy-duty engine cooling system.  In terms of convenience equipment, air conditioning, power steering, choice of radio systems, leather or corduroy seats, tinted glass, tilt steering, light group and visibility group were offered. Also, the exterior could have been dressed with a vinyl top, styled steel wheels, a front spoiler and bumper guards.  ENGINE  …the new-for-1971 401 employed a forged crank and rods; all used cast-aluminum pistons. A dual exhaust system was standard with the 401.   TRANSMISSION For 1971, an Automatic Chrysler-produced “Torque Command”  727 for the 401.   INTERIOR  Rather than a bench, vinyl bucket seats came standard in the AMX, along with a center console available in four different colors. Vinyl could have been upgraded to leather or corduroy fabric. The curved cockpit-style instrument panel could have been optioned with the Rallye-Pac that would provide a combination clock/tach dubbed “tick-tach”; the Rallye-Pac was included with the “Go” Package. The two-spoke steering wheel used for ’71 gave way to a racier three-spoke wheel for 1972.  CHASSIS AMC’s unit-body platform utilized an independent front suspension system with an anti-roll bar, complemented by a rear leaf-sprung suspension. Though the AMX had a firmer system than its standard Javelin siblings, it could have been upgraded to heavy-duty status via the Handling or Go Package options.

This is not a WRX that has been thrashed. It’s in great condition and has had no major issues over the course of its life. The powertrain is also basically stock. I did flash a stage 1 Cobb tune early on, but removed it after ~6 months because the fuel economy was worse and I was only using the car as a commuter. I still have the accessport and would be happy to include it with the car if desired.   I have seen similar mileage WRX hatches sell for close to 20K, so I believe 15K is a fair price and am relatively firm on that number. I’m looking for a no-hassle transaction and for the car to go to a good owner. Please provide your phone number or email with your inquiry. I can send more details or pictures upon request, and would be happy to do a pre-purchase inspection and provide a full service history once you have seen the car in person. description: This 1986 Toyota 4Runner is a first-generation example riding on Toyota's then-new independent front suspension (IFS) — 1986 was the first model year Toyota moved 4WD trucks and 4Runners away from the solid front axle. It has been in my hands since 1998 and used as a daily driver ever since, all while doing exactly what a first-generation 4Runner was built to do: it has served as a camping rig on trips throughout California, Oregon, and Washington, as well as into Mexico, riding on 31" tires and a set of vintage American Racing alloy wheels. Now showing 297,000 miles, the truck has been maintained almost exclusively by Yarnell's Service Center of Mountain View, CA, a local shop that services Toyotas only, and I can provide a continuous paper trail of invoices dating back to 2004.  **Highlights**  - First-generation 4Runner (1986), VIN JT4RN62D2G0063803, independent front suspension (IFS), part-time 4WD - Owned and daily-driven by the same owner since 1998, with camping trips throughout California, Oregon, Washington, and Mexico - 31" tires on a set of vintage American Racing alloy wheels - 297,000 miles, with the vast majority of maintenance performed by Yarnell's Service Center, a Toyota-only specialist shop, with invoices on file back to 2004 - Fully synthetic motor oil used since I took possession in 1998 - Engine overhaul with Toyota factory OEM short block, new clutch assembly and hydraulics, front axles, and valve grind/resurface — 2/28/11 at 220,157 miles - 5-speed manual transmission rebuilt by an outside transmission specialist — 4/6/17 at approximately 251,000 miles - California smog-legal LCE exhaust header; currently smog-certified and registered - JW Speaker industrial-grade LED headlight replacements - OEM Toyota replacement parts used throughout the Yarnell's service history - Original rear seat cushions/hardware and an OEM steering wheel included with the sale - Clean title - Can furnish the Vehicle Window Sticker and Build Sheet on request  **Wheels & Tires**  The truck rides on a set of vintage American Racing alloy wheels wrapped in 31" tires, a period-correct look that suits both the daily-driver duty and the camping trips this 4Runner has racked up over the years.  **Drivetrain**  The truck retains its 5-speed manual gearbox, rebuilt by an outside transmission specialist in April 2017 at roughly 251,000 miles after I reported noise under Yarnell's inspection that March. The engine received a full overhaul at Yarnell's on 2/28/11 at 220,157 miles, including a Toyota factory OEM short block, new clutch assembly and hydraulics, replacement front axles, and a valve grind and resurface — meaning the current bottom end has covered roughly 76,000 miles since installation. A California smog-legal header was fitted in 2000, and the truck is currently smog-certified and registered for on-road use. I run fully synthetic motor oil since taking ownership in 1998, well ahead of when synthetic became common practice for older Toyota trucks, at 4,000 mile intervals.

description: Hello CL I have a 1961 Oldsmobile 98 "Holiday" sedan for sale. Price is $4K OBO, so make an offer. I need paint $ for a different project, and this car is in my way. This car could be considered a project, or you could make it a daily driver. I used it daily from Oakland to SF for a few months myself. I've had this car since early 2022, and picked it up from a guy in Petaluma. He had done carburetor replacement, radiator coring, and just general mechanical things while he had it. I bought it intending to do body and interior, but too many other projects got in the way. The only thing i did mechanically was replacement of the fuel pump. Runs great and sounds awesome through a cherry bomb under the rear seats. The interior floor is stripped, and I have a full carpet set for it as well as Oldsmobile floor mats. All the upholstery is readily avail as are door cards and all that jazz if you wanted toi go that route. It comes with a ton of parts including sheet metal (hood, decklid), front shocks, bumpers, (i believe) ALL the chrome, Seat belts, extra headlight buckets and assemblies, hubcaps, fender skirts, carburetors, and a bunch of other things. Theres enough extra parts to fill the interior of a VW Thing (not for sale) sitting in my garage. The front seat was ripped and leaking stuffing, so I took out the old foam and replaced it with some cushion parts I had laying around. Its not the prettiest, but its much comfier than it was. The rear tires are larger than the front, so thats fun. The springs have been cut all around, so its basically a lowrider that you cant lift up. Its not great at speed bumps for this reason. This vehicle has a ton of potential  and is a great runner as is. Personally id either clear coat the patina and replace the chrome, or flat black the whole damn thing. Maybe airbags? I have no body or interior skills, but if you do, the mechanical is pretty tip top Hit me up for photos, questions, or to come check it out. Registration through 11/26 and clean title. description: 1951 Nash Statesman Super Airflyte  The owner of this Nash Airflyte we have nicknamed The Foster Father of  Orphan Cars as he's a collector of orphan brands such as Nash, Studebaker, AMC, DMC, etc.  He purchased this car as part of a package deal in order to get another car. After a few years of ownership, he's decided it time for this one to fly the coop.  In dealing with the widow who sold him the cars, she unfortunately didn't know any history on the car. It is apparent however, that the car was restored at some point. The seafoam green paint is in very good condition, it could use a good cut and buff but is very presentable as it sits. There are several imperfections throughout, called out in photos, however, at 10 feet most are indiscernible. The chrome shines very nicely, and again, up close, one will fine small faults/pitting. These may respond to the old tinfoil and Coke method of polishing.  The interior is the same. It's in too good condition for it to be original, but it is done in original fabrics so it appears original/stock. There are couple small holes in the back seat and a stain on the driver's seat, an attempt was made to remove it but I feel it needs a special oil stain remover and a steam cleaning. There is also some light staining on the rear seat. The glass is all in very condition, windows all open and close. A special feature of the Nash automobiles was the fully reclining front seats. The car was pitched as a traveling family's sedan. Drive during the day, recline the seats into a double bed and sleep at night, get up refreshed and hit the road again.  The oil pressure and temp gauges work, the fuel gauge is sporadic. The horn does not work, nor do the lights, blinkers or wipers. The overdrive was said to work, however, due to the lights and no registration, the car was not driven on the road to see if the OD does indeed operate correctly.  Turn the key , press the clutch pedal to the floor (the starter button is behind the pedal) and the engine fires right up, the big flat head inline 6 purring smoothly, making over 60 PSI oil pressure. It sat idling for over 20 minutes and didn't exhibit any overheat issues and the gauge sat solidly in the middle. The date code on the engine suggests this is the original engine, unknown as to if it's been rebuilt but 60 PSI oil pressure shows the internals are in very condition, the odometer shows 43000 miles, that may be correct.   The clutch grabs firmly and the 3 on the tree manual shifts easily.  Around the lot I was able to get the car into all three gears with ease, the car runs and drives well, brakes are solid and stop this big car as they should.  The 3 speed sends the torque to the 3 link, coil sprung rear which gives a very nice ride .. almost like you're flying.  Underneath, the Nash Specific Bonderite undercoating seems to have done it's job. While there is indeed some surface rust, there is no rot, no holes where they're not supposed to be. Some of it has peeled as seen in the photos.  When the current owner got the car, it wouldn't start. The fuel filter was replaced, the plugs were replaced and the 6V  voltage regulator, new gas was added along with some BG gas additive. That seemed to do the trick.  Unfortunately what is seen throughout the car are the effects of sitting. The car sat for many years as part of the collection out west where the car came from.   However, what is now presented for sale is a solid, great running-driving automobile that will be the only one at your local cars and coffees, cruise nights and cars shows.  Track down the electrical issues, do some cleaning/polishing and take her out flyi - I mean driving.  These old Nash's despite being fairly rare, are not expensive cars and are an awesome, inexpensive way into the collector car world. 4 doors and big seats mean there's plenty of room for the entire family.  Asking price on this Statesman Super Airflyte is only $10,500.   Any questions,  for several hundred additional photos and several videos, to arrange a time to see her in person or just to make an offer, please don't hesitate to contact me.   Thank you for the interest!

The transmission is an NV3550 and it can easily be replaced with a remanufactured one, or it can even be replaced with a heavier duty AX15. The Ugly The fenders are after market metal and can be used as is but probably should be replaced. I fought the rust and the rust one.  Body itself is ok with just small surface rust in places.

description: 1989 F0rd F250 7.3 IDI with ATS Turbo kit. 237k miles. Runs and drives but needs work.  The engine I believe was replaced with a 1991 motor since when I got it the seller said it had been replaced at 160k miles. Recent Lil Moose injection pump, glow plugs and I made a new glow plug harness, brand new alternator. Owned since 2004, bought out of Arizona, so you can imagine the paint is faded. Briefly, the main issue is the transmission will grind if you are not very careful on shifting. It could be just the throw out bearing, I installed the small firewall reinforcement kit a while back. The clutch and flyweel is the single mass LUK kit, I'm just gonna guess it has around 40k on it.  Its going to need a rear drum job. The batteries start and work but will need to get done sometime. Paint: somewhat present. Some rust above the windows.  Interior: it was a work truck, mismatched panels. Front driver seat needs work. I took out the rear seat and cooked up a little wooden bench for tools etc. I have the original rear bench seat but it down in the bay area along with some extra parts (i.e. brake rotor spare caliper and I cant remember what else) Subwoofer: not included (too powerful for the general population and even made my ex army ranger  friend sick) Rear cab over: has a dent and needs at least two new struts. They are pretty cheap Bed: has a plastic liner.  Basically, I'm tired of working on it and I don't feel like dropping the tranny another time. Too many other projects.  I'll get some more pictures after I clean my tools and stuff out.  Title in hand.  Price is best offer.  Send an email with your contact info and I'll give you a call and answer any questions.

NEW TOYO OPEN COUNTRY AT3 10-PLY TIRES. Regular cab long box 4x4 three-quarter tons in this condition are hard to find at any price.  This is the configuration people actually go looking for and rarely find. Regular cab, 8-foot box, 4x4, gas. No back seat to fill with junk, no short bed to fight with. The full 8-foot box takes 4x8 sheet goods flat on the floor, 16-foot lumber with the tailgate down, a full pallet, two dirt bikes or sleds, or a fifth-wheel pin set where it belongs instead of crowded against the cab. The single-piece cab is the stiffest, lightest body Ram builds on this platform, which is why this truck carries a 10,000 pound GVWR and a factory payload rating of 3,690 pounds. It came out of a Montana and Wyoming commercial fleet and it was a manager and foreman truck, not a crew truck that gets handed to a different driver every week. It shows in the way it drives and in the 16 service records.  The 6.4L Heavy Duty HEMI puts out 410 horsepower and 429 lb-ft, runs on 87 octane, and has no DEF tank, no diesel particulate filter and no regeneration cycles to plan your life around. At Front Range altitude and in cold weather it just starts and goes. Behind it is the 8HP75-LCV eight-speed automatic, the ZF-based unit Ram put in the gas HD trucks, and it is the reason this truck tows better than the numbers suggest. Deep first gear for getting a loaded trailer moving, tight ratio spacing so the engine stays in its torque band on a long grade instead of searching for gears, a locking torque converter that keeps heat out of the fluid, plus Tow/Haul and grade braking. It is a strong, proven, low-drama transmission. Add the factory 4.10 rear end, the anti-spin limited slip differential, the Class V hitch and the integrated trailer brake controller, and this truck is rated for roughly 17,400 pounds conventional when properly equipped.  Inside it is a work interior done right and it is genuinely clean. Heavy duty vinyl 40/20/40 split bench with Mopar rubber mats over a full vinyl floor, so it hoses out and nothing stains or holds a smell. The Tradesman Level 1 group adds remote keyless entry, power windows with front one-touch down, speed sensitive power locks and the overhead console. description: I bought this BMW for my son; my plan was to restore it back to the best possible condition so he wouldn't have to deal with any issues. I spent many thousands of dollars to have Euro Mobile service this vehicle and get it to the best possible condition. After all the money I spent and the laundry list of items done to it, I was sure my son would love it, but it turns out his gratitude to everything fell short so guess what? I'm going to sell this vehicle to someone who will appreciate a vehicle that is in a better condition than what a dealership would and could ever offer someone. Here's what Euro Mobile did: • Engine harmonic balancer replaced with four new mounting bolts. • New Duralast drive belt. • Battery replaced with a new Duralast Platinum battery. • Engine oil and filter service completed using Liqui Moly Top Tec 6600 0W-20 synthetic oil and a new OEM BMW oil filter.  • Automatic transmission serviced with a new integrated oil pan/filter assembly, gasket, mounting hardware, and fresh Liqui Moly transmission fluid. • Cooling system serviced. Coolant flush and replace with BMW coolant. • Fuel tank breather/purge valve replaced. • K&N engine air filter installed • Engine cooling system was also checked with a head gasket leak detector and pressure tested to ensure no coolant leaks. • Engine inspected from top to bottom for any oil leaks, bone dry. • Front and rear brake rotors and ceramic brake pads replaced. • Front and rear brake pad wear sensors replaced. • Brake fluid flush and replaced with Bosch ESI6 brake fluid. • Both front ABS wheel-speed sensors were replaced. • New front windshield professionally installed. • New windshield wiper blades installed, along with fresh bug removing washer fluid. • Genuine BMW passenger side taillight assembly replaced. • Rear center bumper cover molding replaced. • Radiator upper guard/cover panel replaced. • Exterior/interior plastic trim treated  • Vehicle paint washed, paint corrected/scratch removal, polished, and sealed with 3-month ceramic sealant. • BMW navigation display replaced, restoring the primary iDrive information and navigation screen. • Interior lighting upgraded with BMW LED lamps, including four ground/puddle lights and two front ambient-light units. • Interior door-handle assemblies were replaced to address the common deterioration of the original BMW soft touch handles. • Saddle Brown leather surfaces professionally color restored using BMW matched leather dye. • Cabin air filter replaced. I have all of the documentation to prove all of this was done; most dealerships and resellers will just change the oil/filter and make the appearance look nice leaving you to take care of the rest of the issues when you find out about them. Whoever buys this vehicle will have a dependable long-lasting BMW that also looks very nice (almost brand new). OBO
